newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends down in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends down in dull trading.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended down in sluggish trading on Friday, with investors staying on the sidelines on the eve of China's National Day holiday, traders said.

The key October contract ended at 2,200 yuan ($265) per tonne, down 40 yuan. It opened at that level and stayed there for the whole session. December fell 25 to 2,055 yuan. Combined volume fell to 600 tonnes from 1,900 at the previous session.
Traders said most investors did not want to hold positions during the holiday.
China's National Day holiday will last five days from September 28 to October 2. Trading will resume on October 3.
"The trading volume was only 600 tonnes for the whole session, which indicated most investors had lost interest in trading," one trader said.
There was no trading on the exchange on Wednesday and Thursday because of a lack of interest from investors.
Traders expect rice to trade in thin volume after the holiday.
